correctness.rationale: Jordan signed-measure decomposition identifies the exact BV norm with step errors. Negative-binomial survival equals the beta-prime CDF I_(x/(1+x))(j,n); integration by parts yields E_{n,j}, whose strict convexity forces cell-endpoint maxima. Full-line absolute moments minus endpoint overshoot produce the universal 2/sqrt(pi) asymptotic. Uniform gamma-ratio CLT and moderate-deviation Gaussian overshoot balance prove boundary retreat coefficient sqrt(2). Standalone checker cross-checks negative-binomial tails, direct quadrature, and convex endpoint bounds; finite tests do not replace infinite proof.

value.rationale: For discontinuous half-line data the operator norm rather than a pointwise order bound is the natural worst-case approximation measure on a fixed observation window. The finite beta-prime formula makes it computable for every degree, while the sharp 2/sqrt(pi) coefficient and √2 logarithmic retreat locate the hardest discontinuities just inside the observed right edge. The new exact statistic is motivated by negative-binomial point sampling and differs quantitatively from Poisson/Kantorovich analogues; it is not an arbitrary finite slice.
